+# Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+## Overview
+
+Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) is the sparse attention of
+[Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). An indexer selects up to 512 complete
+4-token key blocks per query, and each query attends to those blocks plus the tokens of its own incomplete block.
+
+`cudnn.QSA` provides the attention backward pass for Blackwell (SM100), implemented as CuTe DSL kernels. The indexer,
+the attention forward pass and the indexer loss are not included.
+
+## Semantics
+
+For query `i`, query head `h` (KV head `h // 12`) and each selected token `j` of row `i`, with
+`S_ij = q_i · k_j / 16` and `P_ij = exp(S_ij - lse_ih)`:
+
+```text
+Delta_i = rowsum(dO_i * O_i)
+dS_ij   = P_ij * (dO_i · v_j - Delta_i)
+dQ_i    = (1/16) * sum_j dS_ij k_j
+dK_j    = (1/16) * sum_{i, h in the KV group} dS_ij q_i
+dV_j    = sum_{i, h in the KV group} P_ij dO_i
+```
+
+## Index layout
+
+`topk_idxs` is the `(T, 2051)` int32 matrix of selected token ids, shared by all heads. Row `i` holds, in order:
+
+1. `nsel = min((i + 1) // 4, 512)` complete blocks in any order, each the four consecutive ids `4b, ..., 4b + 3`
+   with `4b + 3 <= i`
+2. the `(i + 1) % 4` tokens of the incomplete block, `4 * ((i + 1) // 4), ..., i`
+3. `-1` in the remaining columns
+
+This is the layout the Qwen3.8 indexer produces. The kernels do not validate it, and rows that deviate from it give
+wrong gradients.
+
+## Support surface
+
+- SM100 (compute capability 10.0) with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0`.
+- 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 256 and softmax scale 1/16.
+- One sequence of `1 <= T <= 349525` tokens.
+
+| Tensor | Shape | Dtype |
+|---|---|---|
+| `q`, `out`, `dout`, `dq` | `(T, 24, 256)` | bf16 |
+| `k`, `v`, `dk`, `dv` | `(T, 2, 256)` | bf16 |
+| `lse` | `(T, 24)` | fp32, natural-log LSE of the scaled scores |
+| `topk_idxs` | `(T, 2051)` | int32 |
+
+All tensors must be contiguous and on the same CUDA device. `check_support()` raises `NotImplementedError` or
+`ValueError` for anything else.
+
+## Numerics
+
+- MMA operands are bf16 (`P` and `dS` are rounded to bf16). All accumulation is fp32, and the outputs are cast to
+  bf16 at the end.
+- dK, dV and part of dQ are reduced with fp32 atomics, so results are not bitwise reproducible.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend
+```

@@ -0,0 +1,1961 @@
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) backward for SM100, written with the CuTe DSL primitives."""
+
+import math
+
+import torch
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cutlass.experimental.cuda as cuda
+from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda_driver
+from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_compact_tensor, make_fake_stream
+from cutlass.experimental import primitives as prims
+
+from cudnn.api_base import ws_align
+
+I32 = cutlass.Int32
+F32 = cutlass.Float32
+BF16 = cutlass.BFloat16
+
+HQ = 24
+HKV = 2
+GQ = 12
+D = 256
+W = 2051
+TOPK = 512
+SCALE = 1.0 / 16.0
+LOG2E = 1.4426950408889634
+
+NTHREADS = 512
+# Blocks per chunk fill 8 * CHB of the 128 MMA rows, and 13 is the largest count whose two K stages and one V stage
+# fit in shared memory. Rows past 8 * CHB alias the next region, which for V includes fp32 staging that may decode as NaN.
+CHB = 13
+
+
+OFF_Q = 0  # [4 slabs][24 head rows x 128 B] with a 128-byte swizzle (SW128), rows 0-11 for KV head 0
+OFF_DO = 12288
+QSLAB = 3072
+OFF_K = 24576  # MMA row = 8 * block + 2 * token + head, so one block covers both KV heads
+BLK_SMEM = 4096  # a gathered block is exactly [4 slabs][8 rows x 128 B] of SW128 atoms, so its TMA box needs no repack
+SLAB = 1024
+K_STAGE = CHB * BLK_SMEM  # blocks sit at the 8-row-group stride of the MMA operand
+OFF_V = OFF_K + 2 * K_STAGE
+OFF_DS = OFF_V + K_STAGE
+DS_BYTES = 6144
+NDRAIN = 8
+EP_BYTES = 4096
+OFF_EP = OFF_DS + DS_BYTES
+SMEM_BYTES = OFF_EP + NDRAIN * EP_BYTES
+
+TM_S = 0
+TM_DP = 32
+TM_PT = 64
+TM_DST = 96
+TM_DQ = 128
+TM_SL = 192
+NSL = 5  # the most 64-column dV/dK slices that fit in the 512 TMEM columns after TM_SL
+L2_EVICT_FIRST = 0x12F0000000000000  # createpolicy encodings of the L2 evict-first and evict-last priorities
+L2_EVICT_LAST = 0x14F0000000000000
+TM_COLS = 512
+
+Q_BOX_BYTES = 24 * 128
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _wait(bar, parity):
+    while not prims.mbarrier_try_wait_parity(bar, parity):
+        pass
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _st_async16(dst, v4, mbar):
+    # st.async stores 16 B from registers into a peer CTA's shared memory and completes them on the peer's mbarrier.
+    prims.inline_ptx(
+        "st.async.shared::cluster.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.v4.b32 [{$r0}], {{$r1}, {$r2}, {$r3}, {$r4}}, [{$r5}];",
+        read_only_args=[dst, v4[0], v4[1], v4[2], v4[3], mbar],
+    )
+
+
+def _desc(addr, lbo, sbo, swz):
+    return prims.Tcgen05SmemDesc.build(start_address=addr, leading_byte_offset=lbo, stride_byte_offset=sbo, layout=swz)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _qmeta(qi):
+    ncb = (qi + 1) >> 2
+    nsel = ncb
+    if nsel > TOPK:
+        nsel = I32(TOPK)
+    ntail = (qi + 1) - (ncb << 2)
+    nblk = nsel
+    if ntail > 0:
+        nblk = nsel + 1
+    return ncb, nsel, ntail, nblk
+
+
+# The tail block of the last queries may reduce exact zeros up to 3 tokens past T, so the sparse dK/dV
+# accumulators carry PAD fp32 elements of slack.
+PAD = 4 * HKV * D
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _bwd_slice(j, cgb, pb, b_le, b_lf, tmem_raw, d_do_mn, d_q_mn, idesc_kv):
+    gs = cgb * 8 + j
+    slot = gs % NSL
+    _wait(b_le.subview(slot), ((gs // NSL) & 1) ^ 1)
+    prims.tcgen05_fence(prims.Tcgen05Fence.AFTER_THREAD_SYNC)
+    d_sl = prims.make_tmem_ptr(tmem_raw + (TM_SL + slot * 64), F32)
+    if prims.elect_sync():
+        for k2 in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+            if cutlass.const_expr(j < 4):
+                a_op = prims.make_tmem_ptr(tmem_raw + (TM_PT + pb * 16 + k2 * 8), BF16)
+                b_op = d_do_mn.advance_start_address(j * QSLAB + k2 * 2048)
+            else:
+                a_op = prims.make_tmem_ptr(tmem_raw + (TM_DST + pb * 16 + k2 * 8), BF16)
+                b_op = d_q_mn.advance_start_address((j - 4) * QSLAB + k2 * 2048)
+            prims.tcgen05_mma(
+                prims.Tcgen05MMAKind.F16,
+                prims.CTAGroup.CTA_1,
+                d_sl,
+                a_op,
+                b_op,
+                idesc_kv,
+                k2 > 0,
+            )
+        prims.tcgen05_commit(b_lf.subview(slot), group=prims.CTAGroup.CTA_1)
+
+
+# Query-major path: both KV heads share each M=128 MMA through block-diagonal masking, so every gathered K/V
+# block serves all 24 query heads with one load.
+@cute.kernel
+def qsa_bwd_sparse_kernel(
+    tma_q: cutlass.GridConstant[cuda.TensorMap],
+    tma_do: cutlass.GridConstant[cuda.TensorMap],
+    tma_k: cutlass.GridConstant[cuda.TensorMap],
+    tma_v: cutlass.GridConstant[cuda.TensorMap],
+    tma_sparse_dv_acc: cutlass.GridConstant[cuda.TensorMap],
+    g_lse: cute.Tensor,
+    g_delta: cute.Tensor,
+    g_dq: cute.Tensor,
+    g_sparse_dk_acc: cute.Tensor,
+    g_sparse_blocks: cute.Tensor,
+    g_sparse_pass_offsets: cute.Tensor,
+    T: I32,
+    nctas: I32,
+    qlo: I32,
+    NP: I32,
+):
+    # K/V blocks are streamed once per item, while the dK/dV accumulators of the pass are revisited
+    hint_ld = cutlass.Int64(L2_EVICT_FIRST)
+    hint_red = cutlass.Int64(L2_EVICT_LAST)
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+    bid, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    warp = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+    lane = tidx % 32
+
+    # The dense pair grid is a programmatic dependent launch (PDL) that backfills SMs released by sparse load imbalance.
+    prims.griddepcontrol("launch_dependents")
+
+    smem = cutlass.Array(I32, SMEM_BYTES // 4, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=1024)
+    b_qf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_qe = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_kf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 2, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_ke = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 2, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_vf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_ve = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_sf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_pf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 2, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_pe = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 2, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_lf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, NSL, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_le = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, NSL, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_dqf = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    b_dqe = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int64, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=8)
+    tmem_slot = cutlass.Array(I32, 1, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem, alignment=4)
+
+    # dQ^T multiplies the K rows past 8 * CHB by zero dS, so they must be finite and the region is zeroed before any load.
+    # The V rows past 8 * CHB need no such care because the softmax assigns zero to masked P and dS instead of scaling them.
+    zero4 = cutlass.Vector.from_elements([I32(0), I32(0), I32(0), I32(0)], I32)
+    sbase = smem.data_ptr()
+    for it in cutlass.range(tidx, SMEM_BYTES // 16, NTHREADS, unroll=1):
+        (sbase + it * 4).store(zero4, alignment=16)
+
+    if warp == 0:
+        if prims.elect_sync():
+            prims.prefetch_tensormap(tma_q.get_ptr())
+            prims.prefetch_tensormap(tma_do.get_ptr())
+            prims.prefetch_tensormap(tma_k.get_ptr())
+            prims.prefetch_tensormap(tma_v.get_ptr())
+            prims.prefetch_tensormap(tma_sparse_dv_acc.get_ptr())
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_qf, 1)
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_qe, 1)
+            for s in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                prims.mbarrier_init(b_kf.subview(s), 1)
+                prims.mbarrier_init(b_ke.subview(s), 1)
+                prims.mbarrier_init(b_pf.subview(s), 4)
+                prims.mbarrier_init(b_pe.subview(s), 1)
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_sf, 1)
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_vf, 1)
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_ve, 1)
+            for s in cutlass.range_constexpr(NSL):
+                prims.mbarrier_init(b_lf.subview(s), 1)
+                prims.mbarrier_init(b_le.subview(s), 4)
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_dqf, 1)
+            prims.mbarrier_init(b_dqe, 4)
+    if warp == 2:
+        prims.tcgen05_alloc(tmem_slot, TM_COLS, group="cta_1")
+        prims.tcgen05_relinquish_alloc_permit(group="cta_1")
+    prims.fence_mbarrier_init()
+    prims.fence_proxy(prims.Proxy.ASYNC_SHARED, space=prims.SharedSpace.shared_cta)
+    prims.barrier_cta_sync(0)
+
+    tmem_raw = tmem_slot.load()
+    tmem_col0 = tmem_raw & I32(0xFFFF)

+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()

+"""Gather-based fp32 references for Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) and its index layout."""
+
+import torch
+
+H_Q = 24
+H_KV = 2
+GROUP = H_Q // H_KV
+D = 256
+BLOCK = 4
+TOPK_BLOCKS = 512
+W = TOPK_BLOCKS * BLOCK + BLOCK - 1
+SCALE = D**-0.5
+CHUNK = 512
+
+
+def make_topk_idxs(seq_len, generator):
+    """Index rows in the QSA indexer layout, selecting uniformly random complete blocks."""
+    device = generator.device
+    pos = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device)
+    ncb = (pos + 1) // BLOCK
+    nsel = ncb.clamp(max=TOPK_BLOCKS)
+    idx = torch.full((seq_len, W + 1), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    for r0 in range(0, seq_len, 4096):
+        r1 = min(r0 + 4096, seq_len)
+        nb = int(ncb[r1 - 1])
+        if nb == 0:
+            continue
+        scores = torch.rand((r1 - r0, nb), device=device, generator=generator)
+        scores.masked_fill_(torch.arange(nb, device=device)[None, :] >= ncb[r0:r1, None], -1.0)
+        top = scores.topk(min(TOPK_BLOCKS, nb), dim=1).indices
+        top = top.masked_fill(torch.arange(top.shape[1], device=device)[None, :] >= nsel[r0:r1, None], -1)
+        tok = torch.where(top[:, :, None] >= 0, top[:, :, None] * BLOCK + torch.arange(BLOCK, device=device), -1)
+        idx[r0:r1, : tok.shape[1] * BLOCK] = tok.flatten(1)
+    j = torch.arange(BLOCK - 1, device=device)
+    in_tail = j[None, :] < ((pos + 1) % BLOCK)[:, None]
+    idx.scatter_(1, torch.where(in_tail, nsel[:, None] * BLOCK + j, W), torch.where(in_tail, ncb[:, None] * BLOCK + j, -1))
+    return idx[:, :W].to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+
+
+def reference_forward(q, k, v, topk_idxs):
+    """bf16 output and fp32 natural-log LSE of the scaled scores, the backward's saved tensors."""
+    out = torch.empty_like(q)
+    lse = torch.empty((q.shape[0], H_Q), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    kf, vf = k.float(), v.float()
+    for r0 in range(0, q.shape[0], CHUNK):
+        r1 = min(r0 + CHUNK, q.shape[0])
+        idx = topk_idxs[r0:r1].long()
+        flat = idx.clamp(min=0).reshape(-1)
+        ks = kf.index_select(0, flat).view(*idx.shape, H_KV, D)
+        vs = vf.index_select(0, flat).view(*idx.shape, H_KV, D)
+        s = torch.einsum("nhgd,nwhd->nhgw", q[r0:r1].float().view(-1, H_KV, GROUP, D), ks) * SCALE
+        s = s.masked_fill(~(idx >= 0)[:, None, None, :], float("-inf"))
+        row_lse = s.logsumexp(-1)
+        o = torch.einsum("nhgw,nwhd->nhgd", torch.exp(s - row_lse[..., None]), vs)
+        out[r0:r1] = o.reshape(-1, H_Q, D).to(out.dtype)
+        lse[r0:r1] = row_lse.reshape(-1, H_Q)
+    return out, lse
+
+
+def reference_backward(q, k, v, out, dout, lse, topk_idxs):
+    """fp32 (dq, dk, dv) from the saved bf16 ``out`` and fp32 ``lse``, the operands the backward consumes.
+
+    Not autograd: rows with few keys cancel in dP - Delta, so a Delta from the unrounded O misses the tolerance.
+    """
+    kf, vf = k.float(), v.float()
+    dq = torch.empty(q.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    dk = torch.zeros(k.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    dv = torch.zeros(v.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    for r0 in range(0, q.shape[0], CHUNK):
+        r1 = min(r0 + CHUNK, q.shape[0])
+        idx = topk_idxs[r0:r1].long()
+        valid = idx >= 0
+        flat = idx.clamp(min=0).reshape(-1)
+        ks = kf.index_select(0, flat).view(*idx.shape, H_KV, D)
+        vs = vf.index_select(0, flat).view(*idx.shape, H_KV, D)
+        qf = q[r0:r1].float().view(-1, H_KV, GROUP, D)
+        dof = dout[r0:r1].float().view(-1, H_KV, GROUP, D)
+        s = torch.einsum("nhgd,nwhd->nhgw", qf, ks) * SCALE
+        p = torch.exp(s.masked_fill(~valid[:, None, None, :], float("-inf")) - lse[r0:r1].view(-1, H_KV, GROUP, 1))
+        delta = (dof * out[r0:r1].float().view(-1, H_KV, GROUP, D)).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
+        ds = p * (torch.einsum("nhgd,nwhd->nhgw", dof, vs) - delta)
+        dq[r0:r1] = (torch.einsum("nhgw,nwhd->nhgd", ds, ks) * SCALE).reshape(-1, H_Q, D)
+        dk.index_add_(0, flat, (torch.einsum("nhgw,nhgd->nwhd", ds, qf) * SCALE).reshape(-1, H_KV, D))
+        dv.index_add_(0, flat, torch.einsum("nhgw,nhgd->nwhd", p, dof).reshape(-1, H_KV, D))
+    return dq, dk, dv
+
+
+def make_inputs(seq_len, seed, grad_scale=1.0, device="cuda"):
+    """Random QSA backward operands. ``grad_scale`` shrinks dO to training-like gradient magnitudes."""
+    generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
+
+    def randn(*shape):
+        return torch.randn(shape, device=device, generator=generator, dtype=torch.float32).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    q, k, v = randn(seq_len, H_Q, D), randn(seq_len, H_KV, D), randn(seq_len, H_KV, D)
+    dout = (torch.randn((seq_len, H_Q, D), device=device, generator=generator) * grad_scale).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    topk_idxs = make_topk_idxs(seq_len, generator)
+    out, lse = reference_forward(q, k, v, topk_idxs)
+    return {"q": q, "k": k, "v": v, "out": out, "dout": dout, "lse": lse, "topk_idxs": topk_idxs}
+
+
+def assert_grads_close(name, actual, expected, rel_l2_tol=1e-2, row_rel_tol=5e-2, row_floor=0.1):
+    """Global relative L2 error plus a per-(token, head) row bound that catches localized errors.
+
+    Both bounds are relative because gradient magnitudes vary by orders of magnitude across rows.
+    """
+    a, e = actual.float(), expected.float()
+    assert torch.isfinite(a).all(), f"{name} has non-finite values"
+    err = a - e
+    rel_l2 = float(err.norm() / e.norm().clamp_min(1e-30))
+    row_ref = e.norm(dim=-1)
+    row_rel = err.norm(dim=-1) / (row_ref + row_floor * row_ref.pow(2).mean().sqrt()).clamp_min(1e-30)
+    worst = float(row_rel.max())
+    assert rel_l2 <= rel_l2_tol, f"{name}: relative L2 error {rel_l2:.3e} > {rel_l2_tol}"
+    assert worst <= row_rel_tol, f"{name}: worst row error {worst:.3e} > {row_rel_tol} at row {divmod(int(row_rel.argmax()), row_rel.shape[1])}"

+# Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+## Overview
+
+Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) is the sparse attention of
+[Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). An indexer selects up to 512 complete
+4-token key blocks per query, and each query attends to those blocks plus the tokens of its own incomplete block.
+
+`cudnn.QSA` provides the attention backward pass for Blackwell (SM100), implemented as CuTe DSL kernels. The indexer,
+the attention forward pass and the indexer loss are not included.
+
+## Semantics
+
+For query `i`, query head `h` (KV head `h // 12`) and each selected token `j` of row `i`, with
+`S_ij = q_i · k_j / 16` and `P_ij = exp(S_ij - lse_ih)`:
+
+```text
+Delta_i = rowsum(dO_i * O_i)
+dS_ij   = P_ij * (dO_i · v_j - Delta_i)
+dQ_i    = (1/16) * sum_j dS_ij k_j
+dK_j    = (1/16) * sum_{i, h in the KV group} dS_ij q_i
+dV_j    = sum_{i, h in the KV group} P_ij dO_i
+```
+
+## Index layout
+
+`topk_idxs` is the `(T, 2051)` int32 matrix of selected token ids, shared by all heads. Row `i` holds, in order:
+
+1. `nsel = min((i + 1) // 4, 512)` complete blocks in any order, each the four consecutive ids `4b, ..., 4b + 3`
+   with `4b + 3 <= i`
+2. the `(i + 1) % 4` tokens of the incomplete block, `4 * ((i + 1) // 4), ..., i`
+3. `-1` in the remaining columns
+
+This is the layout the Qwen3.8 indexer produces. The kernels do not validate it, and rows that deviate from it give
+wrong gradients.
+
+## Support surface
+
+- SM100 (compute capability 10.0) with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0`.
+- 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 256 and softmax scale 1/16.
+- One sequence of `1 <= T <= 349525` tokens.
+
+| Tensor | Shape | Dtype |
+|---|---|---|
+| `q`, `out`, `dout`, `dq` | `(T, 24, 256)` | bf16 |
+| `k`, `v`, `dk`, `dv` | `(T, 2, 256)` | bf16 |
+| `lse` | `(T, 24)` | fp32, natural-log LSE of the scaled scores |
+| `topk_idxs` | `(T, 2051)` | int32 |
+
+All tensors must be contiguous and on the same CUDA device. `check_support()` raises `NotImplementedError` or
+`ValueError` for anything else.
+
+## Numerics
+
+- MMA operands are bf16 (`P` and `dS` are rounded to bf16). All accumulation is fp32, and the outputs are cast to
+  bf16 at the end.
+- dK, dV and part of dQ are reduced with fp32 atomics, so results are not bitwise reproducible.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend
+```
